section.title: Node.js vs Django vs Spring Boot — Backend Frameworks
section.subtitle: Three ways to build a backend: Express, Django and Spring Boot compared on structure, routing, ORM, APIs, auth and deployment.

node.definition: Express is minimalist and unopinionated — you assemble the stack yourself (ORM, auth, validation via middleware). JavaScript everywhere: same language on client and server.

django.definition: Django is batteries-included and convention-driven ("batteries included"). ORM, admin panel, auth, forms and templating ship in the box — less assembly required.
django.code:
# django-admin startproject mysite
# python manage.py startapp polls
# ORM, admin, auth, migrations all built-in

java.definition: Spring Boot is enterprise-grade with convention over configuration. It autoconfigures beans, embeds Tomcat, and offers Spring Data, Security and a huge ecosystem.

node.definition: Express has no enforced structure — typically routes/, models/, middleware/ folders that you design yourself.
node.code:
myapp/
├── server.js
├── routes/
│   └── users.js
├── models/
│   └── user.js
└── package.json

django.definition: Django splits projects into apps, each with models.py, views.py, urls.py, admin.py, migrations/ — a fixed, predictable layout.
django.code:
mysite/
├── manage.py
├── mysite/        # project settings
└── polls/         # app
    ├── models.py
    ├── views.py
    ├── urls.py
    └── migrations/

java.definition: Spring Boot uses Maven/Gradle with src/main/java packages organised by layer (controller, service, repository, model) or by feature.
java.code:
src/main/java/com/example/app/
├── controller/  # REST endpoints
├── service/     # business logic
├── repository/  # DB access
├── model/       # entities
└── App.java     # @SpringBootApplication

pom.xml          # dependencies

node.definition: Express routes match HTTP method + path and call a handler function. Router modules keep routes organised.

django.definition: Django uses urls.py with path()/re_path() mapping URL patterns to view functions or class-based views.
django.code:
# polls/urls.py
from django.urls import path
from . import views

urlpatterns = [
    path('polls/<int:question_id>/', views.detail),
    path('polls/', views.index),
]

java.definition: Spring uses @RestController with annotations like @GetMapping/@PostMapping on methods; paths support path variables and request params.

topics.title: Database & ORM
topics.learn: How each talks to the database.

node.definition: Node has no built-in ORM — you pick one: Sequelize, TypeORM, Prisma or Mongoose (MongoDB). Queries are often written in the ORM's own syntax.

django.definition: Django ships its own ORM — models are Python classes, queries look like Python, and migrations are auto-generated from model changes.
django.code:
# models.py
class Question(models.Model):
    question_text = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    pub_date = models.DateTimeField()

# query in views.py
latest = Question.objects.filter(
    pub_date__year=2024
).order_by('-pub_date')[:5]

java.definition: Spring Data JPA maps Java entities to tables via annotations. Repository interfaces give you CRUD queries for free; JPQL/HQL for complex ones.

node.definition: Express doesn't ship a template engine — you add EJS, Pug or Handlebars, or go full SPA with a separate React/Vue frontend and JSON APIs.

django.definition: Django Templates is built in — HTML files with {{ variables }}, {% tags %} for logic, inheritance via {% extends %}, and automatic XSS escaping.
django.code:
{% extends "base.html" %} {% block content %}

{{ question.question_text }}

{% for choice in question.choice_set.all %}

{{ choice.choice_text }}

{% endfor %} {% endblock %}

java.definition: Spring offers Thymeleaf (server-side HTML), or you return JSON from @RestController and let a SPA handle the UI — the modern default.

node.definition: Express has no built-in auth — you wire Passport.js, JWT (jsonwebtoken) or Auth0. Sessions need middleware like express-session.

django.definition: Django ships full auth: User model, login/logout views, session auth, password hashing, decorators like @login_required and groups/permissions.

java.definition: Spring Security provides auth via config: form login, HTTP Basic, OAuth2 and JWT filters — configured mostly with a SecurityFilterChain bean.

node.definition: Express handlers read req.body/req.params and return res.json() — JSON APIs are the natural fit since JS objects map 1:1 to JSON.

django.definition: Django views return JsonResponse or use Django REST Framework (DRF) for serializers, viewsets and routers — the standard for serious APIs.

java.definition: Spring @RestController returns objects serialized to JSON automatically (Jackson). @RequestBody deserializes request JSON into Java objects.

topics.title: Middleware & Request Pipeline
topics.learn: Code that runs on every request.

node.definition: Express middleware are functions (req, res, next) executed in order — used for logging, body parsing, CORS, auth. Order matters.

django.definition: Django middleware is a list of classes in settings.MIDDLEWARE processing request/response — plus decorators (@login_required) and DRF permission classes.

java.definition: Spring uses servlet Filters and HandlerInterceptors plus AOP aspects — cross-cutting concerns like logging, auth and CORS are configured centrally.

topics.title: Testing & Deployment
topics.learn: How each is tested and shipped.

node.definition: Jest/Mocha + Supertest for unit/integration tests. Deploy as a Node process on any host — Docker, PM2, Vercel, AWS — one language end-to-end.

django.definition: Django's test runner + unittest/pytest. Deploy via gunicorn + nginx, or platforms like Heroku/Railway; settings split dev/prod.
django.code:
# tests.py
from django.test import TestCase

class PollTests(TestCase):
    def test_index(self):
        r = self.client.get('/polls/')
        self.assertEqual(r.status_code, 200)

# deploy: gunicorn mysite.wsgi --bind 0.0.0.0:8000

java.definition: JUnit 5 + Spring Boot Test + MockMvc for tests. Deploy as a fat JAR (java -jar) to any JVM host, or containers via Docker/Jib.
